title: Annotatio VI §.I: Recognized Fraternity — Marburg/Rinteln/Cassel; Sendomir; Reformeds profess; Lutherans held by fear of schism
pass_a_gloss: Whence there is no doubt that, as Fraternity once initiated with these Lutherans was recognized by the Reformed — both in Germany among the Marburgers and Rintelners at Cassel, and in Poland at Sendomir among those of the Augsburg, Bohemian, and Helvetic Confession — so the Reformed even today, as always elsewhere, openly profess that Christian Fraternity stands between them and such Lutherans; and likewise that these Lutherans have joined their hearts and minds with the Reformed in fraternal love, though more secretly, held back from external profession of Fraternity by fear of Schism, lest the remaining Lutherans be split from them.
pass_b_english: So there is no doubt: the Reformed once recognized fraternity with these Lutherans — in Germany at Cassel among Marburgers and Rintelners, and in Poland at Sendomir among Augsburg, Bohemian, and Helvetic confessionists.
They still openly profess that Christian fraternity with such Lutherans.
These Lutherans have joined heart and mind to the Reformed in brotherly love, even if more secretly — held back from an external profession by fear of schism with the rest of their own.
source_text: Unde dubium non est, quòd sicuti Reformatis agnita quondam Lutheranorum horum secum inita Fraternitas, tùm in Germania inter Marpurgenses & Rintelenses, Cassellis, tùm in Polonia inter Augustana, Bohemica & Helvetica Confessionis, Sendomiriae est; Reformati etiam hodieque, ut semper aliàs, cum hujusmodi Lutheranis Fraternitatem Christianam sibi intercedere apertè profitentur; Ita non minus Lutheranos hos, corda animosque suos, cum Reformatis fraterno amore, etsi occultius conjunxisse, ab externa licèt Fraternitatis professione, metu Schismatis, quô reliqui Lutherani à se scinderentur, cohibiti.
notes: Marburg/Rinteln/Cassel; Sendomir; occult fraternity; fear of schism.
